scenes.say: The fastest tyre in Formula One doesn't always win. So why not?
Every round gets three dry compounds. The soft has the most grip and is the quickest over one lap.
But it loses a few hundredths every lap, and then it hits the cliff: the grip goes almost all at once.
And every pit stop costs twenty to twenty-five seconds.
Softs shine on smooth tarmac, where passing is hard, and in the cold. Think Monaco, Singapore and Vegas.
In the heat, on abrasive tarmac and through fast sweeps like these at Silverstone, they're gone in a few laps.
Follow every driver's tyre compound and age live on LapRadar.

title: Soft, medium, hard: why the fastest tyre doesn't always win
